| Primary Actor(s): | System User | Secondary Actor(s): | Cloud Object Storage |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Description:** | Allows any authenticated system user (User, Recycler, Staff, Admin) to view their profile details, update editable contact information (Full Name, Phone Number, Address), and upload an updated avatar image. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | **1\.** The System User is authenticated with an active session. **2\.** The System User is on the Profile Settings screen. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | **\- Success:** Updated profile information and avatar are validated and persisted to the database. **\- Failure:** Profile updates are rejected, unsaved changes are discarded, and an informative error message is displayed. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **NF-01:** The System User navigates to the "Profile Settings" screen. **NF-02:** The system retrieves and renders current profile information (Full Name, Phone Number, Registered Email \[Read-only\], Physical Address, Avatar preview). **NF-03:** The System User modifies editable fields (Name, Phone, Address) or selects a new avatar image. **NF-04:** The system displays an immediate local preview of the avatar and validates input formats. **NF-05:** The System User clicks "Save Changes". **NF-06:** The system uploads the avatar to Cloud Object Storage (if modified), saves the profile data to the database, and displays a success confirmation toast. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flow:** | **AF-01:** At NF-03, if the System User clicks "Cancel" or navigates away without saving, the system discards unsaved entries and preserves the original profile data. |  |  |
| **Extension Flow:** | **ETF-01:** N/A |  |  |
| **Exceptions Flow:** | **EF-01:** At NF-03, if an uploaded avatar file is not in JPG or PNG format, the system displays MSG-CLS-01. **EF-02:** At NF-03, if the avatar file exceeds the maximum allowed upload size, the system displays MSG-CLS-02. **EF-03:** At NF-03, if a mandatory profile field is cleared, the system displays MSG-AUTH-02 under the field. **EF-04:** At NF-03, if an input exceeds the maximum length limit, the system displays MSG-NTF-03. **EF-05:** At NF-05, if the user session has expired, the system invalidates the session, displays MSG-NTF-01, and redirects to the Login screen. |  |  |
| **Business Rule** | **BR-AUTH-08:** Access is role-based. Guests access only public information; each role accesses only its own functions and data. **BR-NTF-03:** Notifications are sent only to the account's verified email; changing the email requires re-verification. |  |  |

###  **8.7 Change Password** {#8.7-change-password}

| Primary Actor(s): | System User | Secondary Actor(s): | Gmail |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Description:** | Allows an authenticated user possessing local credentials to change their account password by verifying their current password, saving a new salted hash, and receiving a security confirmation email. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | **1\.** The System User is logged in with an active session. **2\.** The account has a local password credential (non-OAuth-only). **3\.** The System User is on the "Change Password" tab. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | **\- Success:** The new password hash is saved to the database and a security alert email is dispatched. **\- Failure:** The password update is rejected, the existing password remains unchanged, and an error message is displayed. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **NF-01:** The System User enters Current Password, New Password, and Confirm New Password → clicks "Update Password". **NF-02:** The system verifies the Current Password against the stored cryptographic hash and validates the New Password against complexity policies. **NF-03:** The system updates the password hash in the database, dispatches a security alert email to the registered address via Gmail, and displays a success confirmation toast. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flow:** | **AF-01:** At NF-01, if the account registered exclusively via Google OAuth and has no local password, the system displays an informative notice: "Your account is authenticated via Google. Password management is handled through your Google Account." |  |  |
| **Extension Flow:** | **ETF-01:** N/A |  |  |
| **Exceptions Flow:** | **EF-01:** At NF-01, if any required password field is left empty, the system displays MSG-AUTH-02 under the field. **EF-02:** At NF-01, if the entered Current Password does not match the stored credentials, the system rejects the update and displays MSG-AUTH-01. **EF-03:** At NF-01, if the New Password matches the Current Password, the system displays an in-line error: "New password must be different from current password." **EF-04:** At NF-01, if Confirm New Password does not match the New Password, the system displays an in-line error: "Password confirmation does not match." **EF-05:** At any point, if the session has expired, the system displays MSG-NTF-01 and redirects to the Login screen. |  |  |
| **Business Rule** | **BR-AUTH-04:** After {N} consecutive failed sign-ins, the account is temporarily locked for {M} minutes. **BR-AUTH-05:** A deactivated or suspended account cannot sign in, regardless of password correctness, and all active sessions are invalidated immediately. **BR-NTF-01:** Security and transactional emails (verification, password reset, dispute) cannot be disabled by the user. |  |  |

The system navigates to the dedicated Notification Center page. |  |  |

| **Business Rule** | **BR-NTF-02:** Every status change of a handover or dispute notifies all affected parties. **BR-NTF-05:** Notifications must not contain sensitive data (full contact details, tokens), except one-time verification/reset links. |  |  |

###  **8.9 Logout System** {#8.9-logout-system}

| Primary Actor(s): | System User | Secondary Actor(s): | N/A |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Description:** | Allows an authenticated user to terminate their active session, invalidate refresh tokens, clear client authentication state, and return to unauthenticated public access. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | **1\.** The System User is logged in with an active session token. **2\.** The System User is on any authenticated screen. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | **\- Success:** The active session is revoked, refresh tokens are invalidated, local storage is cleared, and the user is redirected to the public Homepage. **\- Failure:** If a network failure occurs during the logout call, client-side session tokens are forcibly purged and the user is redirected to the Homepage. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **NF-01:** The System User clicks "Sign Out" or "Logout" from the user account menu. **NF-02:** The system displays a confirmation prompt: "Are you sure you want to log out?" **NF-03:** The System User confirms logout. **NF-04:** The system calls the logout endpoint, revokes the refresh token in the database/cache, clears client-side tokens/cookies, and redirects to the public Homepage. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flow:** | **AF-01:** At NF-02, if the System User clicks "Cancel", the system closes the prompt and retains the active session on the current screen. |  |  |
| **Extension Flow:** | **ETF-01:** N/A |  |  |
| **Exceptions Flow:** | **EF-01:** At NF-03, if an API timeout or network drop occurs, the client application forcibly destroys local tokens and redirects to the Homepage. |  |  |
| **Business Rule** | **BR-AUTH-05:** A deactivated or suspended account cannot sign in, regardless of password correctness, and all active sessions are invalidated immediately. **BR-AUTH-08:** Access is role-based. Guests access only public information; each role accesses only its own functions and data. |  |  |

###  **8.10 Manage User & Recycler Accounts** {#8.10-manage-user-&-recycler-accounts}

| Primary Actor(s): | Staff | Secondary Actor(s): |   |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Description:** | Allows an authenticated Staff member to search User and Recycler accounts, view their history, and lock or unlock accounts that violate the policies with a recorded reason, in order to keep the platform safe and trustworthy. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | **1\.** The Staff is authenticated and has an active session with role Staff. **2\.** The Staff has been granted the account management permission. **3\.** The Staff is on the User Management screen. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | **\- View:** The system displays the account profile, history, and complaints. **\- Lock:** The account is suspended, its active sessions are invalidated, and the reason is recorded. **\- Unlock:** The account access is restored and the reason is recorded. **\- Failure:** If any operation fails, the system data remains unchanged and an informative error message is displayed to the Staff. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **View Account NF-01:** The Staff selects "Account Management". **NF-02:** The system displays the account list with filters. **NF-03:** The Staff searches by phone number or email → clicks "View Details". **NF-04:** The system displays the profile, transaction history, and complaints.   **Lock Account NF-05:** The Staff clicks "Lock Account". **NF-06:** The system displays a form for the duration and reason. **NF-07:** The Staff enters the reason → clicks "Confirm". **NF-08:** The system locks the account → invalidates its active sessions → writes an audit log entry → displays MSG-ADM-01.   **Unlock Account NF-05 (from NF-04):** The Staff clicks "Unlock Account". **NF-06:** The system displays a form for the reason. **NF-07:** The Staff enters the reason → clicks "Confirm". **NF-08:** The system restores the account access → writes an audit log entry → displays MSG-ADM-01. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flow:** | **AF-01:** At NF-02, the Staff filters the accounts by role, status, or complaint history. |  |  |
| **Extension Flow:** | **ETF-01:** At NF-06 (Lock/Unlock), if the Staff clicks "Cancel", the system closes the form and keeps the account status unchanged. |  |  |
| **Exceptions Flow:** | **EF-01:** At NF-07, if the reason is missing, the system displays MSG-AUTH-02 and prevents the action. **EF-02:** At NF-05, if the Staff attempts to change another Staff or an Admin account, the system denies the action and displays MSG-ADM-04. **EF-03:** At any point, if the Staff's session has expired, the system displays MSG-NTF-01 and redirects the Staff to the Login page. |  |  |
| **Business Rule** | **BR-AUTH-05:** A deactivated or suspended account cannot sign in, regardless of password correctness, and all active sessions are invalidated immediately. **BR-ADM-03:** Staff may change User/Recycler account status only with a recorded reason, and cannot change Admin or other Staff accounts. **BR-ADM-04:** Accounts with transaction history can only be deactivated, never deleted. **BR-ADM-05:** Every Admin/Staff action on configuration, account status, verification, and dispute decisions is recorded in an immutable audit log. |  |  |

###  **8.11 Manage Staff Accounts** {#8.11-manage-staff-accounts}

| Primary Actor(s): | Admin | Secondary Actor(s): | Gmail |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Description:** | Allows an authorized Admin to create, view, update, and deactivate Staff accounts (Staff cannot self-register), in order to control who has access to the operational functions of the platform. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | **1\.** The Admin is authenticated and has an active session with role Admin. **2\.** The Admin has Staff account management privileges. **3\.** The Admin is on the Staff Account Management screen. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | **\- View:** The system displays the latest list of Staff accounts. **\- Create:** A new Staff account is created and the initial credentials are sent to the Staff by email. **\- Update:** The Staff profile is updated. **\- Deactivate:** The Staff account is set to Inactive and all its active sessions are terminated. **\- Failure:** If any operation fails, the system data remains unchanged and an informative error message is displayed to the Admin. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **View Staff Accounts NF-01:** The Admin navigates to the "Staff Accounts" section. **NF-02:** The system displays the Staff list (Full Name, Corporate Email, Department, Status, Actions).   **Create Staff Account NF-03:** The Admin clicks "Add New Staff". **NF-04:** The system displays the Staff creation form. **NF-05:** The Admin enters the Full Name, Corporate Email, Phone Number, and department → clicks "Save". **NF-06:** The system validates the email uniqueness and the creation policy → creates the account with temporary credentials → sends an onboarding email through Gmail → writes an audit log entry → displays MSG-ADM-03 → refreshes the list.   **Update Staff Account NF-03 (from NF-02):** The Admin clicks "Edit" on a Staff row. **NF-04:** The system displays the form pre-populated with the current data. **NF-05:** The Admin modifies the fields → clicks "Save Changes". **NF-06:** The system validates the input → updates the profile → writes an audit log entry → displays a success confirmation.   **Deactivate Staff Account NF-03 (from NF-02):** The Admin clicks "Deactivate" on a Staff row. **NF-04:** The system displays a confirmation dialog. **NF-05:** The Admin confirms the action. **NF-06:** The system sets the status to Inactive → terminates all active sessions of the account → writes an audit log entry → displays a success notification. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flow:** | **AF-01:** At NF-02, the Admin searches by name or email, or filters by department or status, and the system updates the displayed Staff list. |  |  |
| **Extension Flow:** | **ETF-01:** At NF-05 (Create/Update/Deactivate), if the Admin clicks "Cancel", the system closes the dialog and discards all unsaved entries. |  |  |
| **Exceptions Flow:** | **EF-01:** At NF-06 (Create), if the email already exists on any role of the platform, the system displays an error message and prevents saving. **EF-02:** At NF-06 (Create/Update), if a required field is empty, the system displays MSG-AUTH-02 and prevents saving. **EF-03:** At NF-03 (Deactivate), if the Admin attempts to permanently delete an account with historical operational activity, the system blocks the deletion and only allows deactivation. **EF-04:** At NF-06 (Create), if the onboarding email cannot be delivered, the system displays MSG-NTF-02 and keeps the account created. **EF-05:** At any point, if the Admin's session has expired, the system displays MSG-NTF-01 and redirects the Admin to the Login page. |  |  |
| **Business Rule** | **BR-ADM-01:** Staff and Admin accounts are created only by Admin, with no self-registration; Staff cannot create or modify Admin accounts. **BR-ADM-02:** Roles are separated: Admin handles policy, catalog, leaderboard configuration, Staff accounts, and reports. Staff handles disputes, labeling, verification, reward inventory, survey configuration, and account status. **BR-ADM-04:** Accounts with transaction history can only be deactivated, never deleted. **BR-ADM-05:** Every Admin/Staff action on configuration, account status, verification, and dispute decisions is recorded in an immutable audit log. **BR-AUTH-01:** One email address can be linked to only one account, across both roles (User/Recycler) and both sign-up methods (local/Google). **BR-AUTH-05:** A deactivated or suspended account cannot sign in, regardless of password correctness, and all active sessions are invalidated immediately. |  |  |

###  **8.12 Manage Staff Permissions** {#8.12-manage-staff-permissions}

| Primary Actor(s): | Admin | Secondary Actor(s): |   |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Description:** | Allows an authorized Admin to grant or revoke granular operational permissions of Staff accounts in accordance with the separation of duties, in order to ensure each Staff member only accesses the functions required for the assigned role. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | **1\.** The Admin is authenticated and has an active session with role Admin. **2\.** The target Staff account is in Active status. **3\.** The Admin is on the Staff Permissions Configuration screen. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | **\- Success:** The updated permission matrix is saved and takes effect immediately. The action is recorded in the audit log. **\- Failure:** If any operation fails, the system data remains unchanged, the permission settings are not changed, and an informative error message is displayed to the Admin. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **NF-01:** The Admin navigates to the "Staff Permissions Configuration" screen. **NF-02:** The system displays the active Staff members with their current permissions. **NF-03:** The Admin selects a Staff member. **NF-04:** The system displays the permission matrix (Dispute Resolution, AI Dataset Labeling, Recycler Verification, Reward Inventory, Survey Configuration). **NF-05:** The Admin toggles the permissions in accordance with the role separation → clicks "Save Permissions". **NF-06:** The system validates that no administrative governance right is granted to a Staff account → saves the permissions → writes an audit log entry → displays a success confirmation → refreshes the permission view. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flow:** | **AF-01:** At NF-05, the Admin selects a preset role template (e.g., "Dispute Officer", "AI Data Specialist") and the system fills in the corresponding permissions. |  |  |
| **Extension Flow:** | **ETF-01:** At NF-05, if the Admin clicks "Cancel", the system resets the permissions to the currently saved values without saving any change. |  |  |
| **Exceptions Flow:** | **EF-01:** At NF-06, if the selected permissions would grant an administrative governance right to a Staff account, the system rejects the change and displays MSG-ADM-04. **EF-02:** At NF-05, if a non-Admin account attempts to assign permissions, the system denies the request and displays MSG-ADM-04. **EF-03:** At NF-06, if the target Staff account has been deactivated in the meantime, the system rejects the change and refreshes the list. **EF-04:** At any point, if the Admin's session has expired, the system displays MSG-NTF-01 and redirects the Admin to the Login page. |  |  |
| **Business Rule** | **BR-ADM-01:** Staff and Admin accounts are created only by Admin, with no self-registration; Staff cannot create or modify Admin accounts. **BR-ADM-02:** Roles are separated: Admin handles policy, catalog, leaderboard configuration, Staff accounts, and reports. Staff handles disputes, labeling, verification, reward inventory, survey configuration, and account status. **BR-ADM-05:** Every Admin/Staff action on configuration, account status, verification, and dispute decisions is recorded in an immutable audit log. |  |  |

**9\. Blog Content Management**

### **9.1 Create Blog Post Draft** {#9.1-create-blog-post-draft}

| Primary Actor(s): | Staff | Secondary Actor(s): | Admin |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Description:** | Allows an authenticated Staff member to write articles about green living and waste sorting and either save them as drafts or submit them for Admin approval, in order to publish quality educational content for Users. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | **1\.** The Staff is authenticated and has an active session with role Staff. **2\.** The Staff is on the Blog/News Management screen. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | **\- Draft:** The post is saved internally in Draft status. **\- Submit:** The post status is set to Pending\_Approval, the Admin is notified, and MSG-ADM-06 is displayed. **\- Failure:** If any operation fails, the system data remains unchanged, any uploaded temporary files are discarded, and an informative error message is displayed to the Staff. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **NF-01:** The Staff selects "Blog Posts" → clicks "New Post". **NF-02:** The system displays the rich text editor. **NF-03:** The Staff enters the title, uploads a cover image, and writes the content. **NF-04:** The Staff clicks "Preview" to check the layout. **NF-05:** The Staff clicks "Submit for Approval". **NF-06:** The system validates the input → sets the post status to Pending\_Approval → notifies the Admin → displays MSG-ADM-06. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flow:** | **AF-01:** At NF-05, the Staff clicks "Save Draft" and the system saves the post in Draft status without notifying the Admin. |  |  |
| **Extension Flow:** | **ETF-01:** At NF-03, if the Staff clicks "Cancel", the system discards the unsaved content and returns to the Blog/News Management screen. |  |  |
| **Exceptions Flow:** | **EF-01:** At NF-06, if the title or cover image is missing, the system displays MSG-AUTH-02 and prevents submission. **EF-02:** At NF-03, if the cover image is in an unsupported format or exceeds the size limit, the system displays MSG-CLS-01 or MSG-CLS-02 and rejects the image. **EF-03:** At any point, if the Staff's session has expired, the system displays MSG-NTF-01 and redirects the Staff to the Login page. |  |  |
| **Business Rule** | **BR-ADM-02:** Roles are separated: Admin handles policy, catalog, leaderboard configuration, Staff accounts, and reports. Staff handles disputes, labeling, verification, reward inventory, survey configuration, and account status. **BR-ADM-08:** A blog post authored by Staff must be in Draft or Pending\_Approval status. It is published publicly in the app only after Admin approves it (Approved status). |  |  |

###  **9.2 Approve / Reject Blog Post** {#9.2-approve-/-reject-blog-post}

| Primary Actor(s): | Admin | Secondary Actor(s): | Staff |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Description:** | Allows an authorized Admin to review blog posts written by Staff and either approve them for public publication or reject them back to draft with feedback, in order to ensure the content quality before it reaches Users. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | **1\.** The Admin is authenticated and has an active session with role Admin. **2\.** At least one blog post is in Pending\_Approval status. **3\.** The Admin is on the Blog Moderation Queue screen. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | **\- Approve:** The post status is set to Approved and the post is published to Users. The decision is recorded in the audit log and the Staff is notified. **\- Reject:** The post status is set to Draft with the feedback notes and the Staff is notified. **\- Failure:** If any operation fails, the system data remains unchanged, the post remains in Pending\_Approval status, and an informative error message is displayed to the Admin. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **Approve Post NF-01:** The Admin navigates to the "Blog Moderation Queue". **NF-02:** The system displays the posts awaiting review (title, author, submission date, thumbnail). **NF-03:** The Admin opens a post to preview the full text and media. **NF-04:** The Admin clicks "Approve". **NF-05:** The system sets the post status to Approved and publishes it → writes an audit log entry → notifies the Staff → displays MSG-ADM-05.   **Reject Post NF-04 (from NF-03):** The Admin clicks "Reject". **NF-05:** The system displays a feedback form. **NF-06:** The Admin enters the revision feedback → clicks "Send". **NF-07:** The system sets the post status to Draft → writes an audit log entry → notifies the Staff with the feedback. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flow:** | **AF-01:** At NF-02, the Admin searches the queue by title or author, or sorts it by submission date. |  |  |
| **Extension Flow:** | **ETF-01:** At NF-04 or NF-06, if the Admin closes the preview or clicks "Cancel", the system keeps the post in Pending\_Approval status without any change. |  |  |
| **Exceptions Flow:** | **EF-01:** At NF-06 (Reject), if no feedback is entered, the system displays MSG-AUTH-02 and prevents submission. **EF-02:** At NF-05, if the post was recalled to Draft by the Staff before the decision, the system notifies the Admin that the post is no longer pending and refreshes the queue. **EF-03:** At NF-04, if a non-Admin account attempts to approve a post, the system denies the request and displays MSG-ADM-04. **EF-04:** At any point, if the Admin's session has expired, the system displays MSG-NTF-01 and redirects the Admin to the Login page. |  |  |
| **Business Rule** | **BR-ADM-02:** Roles are separated: Admin handles policy, catalog, leaderboard configuration, Staff accounts, and reports. Staff handles disputes, labeling, verification, reward inventory, survey configuration, and account status. **BR-ADM-05:** Every Admin/Staff action on configuration, account status, verification, and dispute decisions is recorded in an immutable audit log. **BR-ADM-08:** A blog post authored by Staff must be in Draft or Pending\_Approval status. It is published publicly in the app only after Admin approves it (Approved status). |  |  |

## **10\. System Analytics & Reporting** {#10.-system-analytics-&-reporting}

### **10.1 View Dashboard & Analytics** {#10.1-view-dashboard-&-analytics}

| Primary Actor(s): | Admin | Secondary Actor(s): |   |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Description:** | Allows an authorized Admin to monitor platform analytics (waste collection volumes, user growth, handover completion, dispute rate, and AI classification performance) in read-only mode, in order to evaluate the operation of the system and support decisions. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | **1\.** The Admin is authenticated and has an active session with role Admin. **2\.** The system contains completed and confirmed operational records. **3\.** The Admin is on the administration home screen. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | **\- Success:** The system displays the KPI cards and charts calculated from completed and confirmed data. No data is modified. **\- Failure:** If any operation fails, the system data remains unchanged and an informative error message is displayed to the Admin. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **NF-01:** The Admin selects the "Dashboard & Analytics" module on the administration sidebar. **NF-02:** The system queries the completed and confirmed operational records. **NF-03:** The system displays the KPI cards (Total Recycled Waste Weight, Completed Handover Count, New User Registrations, Dispute Rate). **NF-04:** The system displays the analytical charts (Waste Distribution by Material, AI Classification Accuracy Rate, Partner Geographic Density). **NF-05:** The Admin selects a metric card to view its detailed breakdown. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flow:** | **AF-01:** At NF-03, the Admin changes the filters (time period: week / month / quarter / year, waste category, or region) and the system recalculates and updates the charts. |  |  |
| **Extension Flow:** | **ETF-01:** At NF-05, if the Admin closes the detailed view or navigates to another administration screen, the system returns to the dashboard without any change. |  |  |
| **Exceptions Flow:** | **EF-01:** At NF-02, if the database connection fails or the analytics service is unreachable, the system displays an error message. **EF-02:** At NF-02, if no data exists for the selected filters, the system displays an empty-state message. **EF-03:** At any point, if the Admin's session has expired, the system displays MSG-NTF-01 and redirects the Admin to the Login page. |  |  |
| **Business Rule** | **BR-ADM-07:** Dashboard analytics are calculated only from completed and confirmed data, and are read-only. |  |  |

###  **10.2 Export Data Reports** {#10.2-export-data-reports}

| Primary Actor(s): | Admin | Secondary Actor(s): |   |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Description:** | Allows an authorized Admin to export analytical summaries, completed transaction records, waste statistics, and partner metrics as downloadable CSV or Excel reports, in order to support reporting and analysis outside the system. |  |  |
| **Preconditions:** | **1\.** The Admin is authenticated and has an active session with role Admin. **2\.** The Admin has reporting and export privileges. **3\.** The Admin is on the Report Export screen. |  |  |
| **Postconditions:** | **\- Success:** The report file (CSV or Excel) is generated and downloaded, and the export is recorded in the audit log. **\- Failure:** If any operation fails, the system data remains unchanged, no file is generated, and an informative error message is displayed to the Admin. |  |  |
| **Normal Flow:** | **NF-01:** The Admin navigates to the "Export Data Reports" screen. **NF-02:** The Admin selects the report type (Completed Trade Records, Waste Stream Statistics, Recycler Performance Overview). **NF-03:** The Admin sets the filters (Start Date, End Date, Region, Transaction Status). **NF-04:** The Admin selects the file format (CSV or Excel). **NF-05:** The Admin clicks "Export". **NF-06:** The system aggregates the records → excludes or anonymizes personal contact and banking details → writes an audit log entry → starts the file download → displays MSG-ADM-02. |  |  |
| **Alternative Flow:** | **AF-01:** At NF-03, if the Admin does not specify a date range, the system applies the default range of the last 30 days. |  |  |
| **Extension Flow:** | **ETF-01:** At NF-05, if the Admin clicks "Cancel", the system aborts the file generation and keeps the selected filters. |  |  |
| **Exceptions Flow:** | **EF-01:** At NF-06, if no record matches the filters, the system displays a message that no data exists and cancels the download. **EF-02:** At NF-05, if a non-authorized account attempts to export reports, the system denies the request and displays MSG-ADM-04. **EF-03:** At NF-06, if the report generation fails because of a system error, the system displays an error message and no file is downloaded. **EF-04:** At any point, if the Admin's session has expired, the system displays MSG-NTF-01 and redirects the Admin to the Login page. |  |  |
| **Business Rule** | **BR-ADM-05:** Every Admin/Staff action on configuration, account status, verification, and dispute decisions is recorded in an immutable audit log. **BR-ADM-06:** Exported reports contain aggregated or anonymized data by default, exclude personal contact details, and every export is logged. |  |  |

## **1\. User Authentication & Profile Management** {#1.-user-authentication-&-profile-management}

### **1.1 Guest Onboarding & Authentication** {#1.1-guest-onboarding-&-authentication}

#### **1.1.1 Landing Homepage & System Introduction (SCR-GST-01)**

![][image17]

  \*\[Placeholder for UI Mockup / Wireframe: SCR-GST-01 — Hero banner with environmental mission, AI waste classification showcase, value proposition for households & recyclers, and portal navigation bar\]\*

This screen allows a Guest to:

* Learn about household waste recycling workflows, partner networks, and featured environmental blogs.

| Navigation Register User | Action button navigating to the User Registration screen (SCR-GST-02). |
| Navigation Register Recycler | Action button navigating to the Recycler Partner Registration screen (SCR-GST-03). |
| Navigation Sign In | Action button navigating to the System Authentication screen (SCR-GST-04). |

#### **1.1.2 User Account Registration (SCR-GST-02)**

![][image18]

* **Mapped Use Case:** G-02: Register as User  
  \[Content \#1: UI layout (Wireframe or Mockup for the screen)\]  
  \*\[Placeholder for UI Mockup: SCR-GST-02 — Standard registration card with Full Name, Phone, Email, Password, Confirm Password, and Terms checkbox\]\*

This screen allows a Guest to:

* Input personal credentials to establish a standard User account.

* Receive real-time validation feedback on phone number format, email syntax, and password strength.  
* Read and accept the platform Terms of Service and Privacy Policy.  
* Tap "Create Account" to submit registration and trigger an account verification email.

**Field Description:**

| Field Name | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Full Name Input | User's full legal name; alphabetic string, length between 2 and 50 characters; mandatory. |
| Email Address Input | Electronic mail address; standard valid email format (e.g., name@domain.com); maximum 100 characters; mandatory; globally unique. |
| Phone Number Input | Mobile phone number in Vietnam format; 10 digits starting with 0; mandatory; globally unique. |
| Password Input | Account secret password; minimum 8 characters, containing at least 1 uppercase letter, 1 lowercase letter, and 1 numeric digit; mandatory. |
| Confirm Password Input | Password re-entry; must match Password Input exactly. |
| Terms Agreement Checkbox | Consent checkbox acknowledging terms of service; boolean; must be checked (True). |

#### **1.1.3 Recycler Partner Upgrade Application (SCR-USR-17)**

●       Mapped Use Case: U-17: Apply for Recycler Upgrade

\[Content \#1: UI layout (Wireframe or Mockup for the screen)\]

This in-app screen allows an authenticated User (Citizen) to:

| Business Phone Input  | Primary corporate contact number; 10 digits; mandatory.  |
| Address Street Input  | Exact physical street address (house number, street name, ward, district); maximum 150 characters; mandatory.  |
| Map Coordinate Picker  | Spatial geographic coordinates comprising Longitude and Latitude; automatically captured upon pinning location on the map.  |
| License Document Uploader  | Upload component for business registration licenses or identity proof; maximum file size 10 MB; stored securely in Cloudflare R2.  |
| Initial Accepted Categories  | Checklist of supported waste categories; requires selecting at least one valid category pursuant to BR-MTH-03.  |

| Field Name | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Account Identifier Input | Registered Email Address or Mobile Phone Number; maximum 100 characters; mandatory. |
| Login Password Input | Account password string; masked character input; mandatory. |

| Google SSO Button | Action button initiating Google OAuth 2.0 authentication flow over secure transport. |
| Forgot Password Link | Hyperlink navigating to the One-Time Password password recovery workflow. |

## **2\. USER Subsystem (Household Waste Sorters)** {#2.-user-subsystem-(household-waste-sorters)}

### **2.1 AI Waste Classification & Guidance** {#2.1-ai-waste-classification-&-guidance}

#### **2.1.1 AI Waste Scanner Viewfinder (SCR-USR-01)**

![][image22]

* **Mapped Use Case:** U-01: Identify Waste via Photo (UC10)  
  \[Content \#1: UI layout (Wireframe or Mockup for the screen)\]  
  \*\[Placeholder for UI Mockup: SCR-USR-01 — Desktop web waste classification portal on PC featuring dual input modalities: live PC webcam viewfinder with instant capture button, and drag-and-drop file upload zone with interactive image preview and analyze CTA\]\*

This screen allows the Citizen User on the desktop web application (PC / Laptop) to:

* Activate the PC/laptop webcam to capture waste images directly via a real-time video feed with an alignment framing guide.  
* Upload existing waste photos from local PC storage via a responsive drag-and-drop zone or system file browser dialog (File Explorer).  
* Review an instant image preview to verify image sharpness and waste clarity prior to submission.  
* Click "Retake / Replace" to clear the preview buffer and capture or select a different photo.  
* Click "Analyze Waste with AI" to upload the image to Cloudflare R2 storage and trigger model inference.

**Field Description:**

| Field Name | Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| Webcam Viewfinder Feed | Live video stream container rendering camera input from PC/laptop webcam; 16:9 or 4:3 aspect ratio with alignment guide overlay. |
| Webcam Capture Button | Shutter action button capturing the active webcam frame and freezing it into the preview buffer. |
| Drag-and-Drop Upload Area | Interactive drop zone accepting image file uploads from PC local storage; supports image/jpeg, image/png, image/webp; maximum 10 MB. |
| Image Preview Container | Visual container displaying the captured or uploaded photo before initiating analysis. |
| Retake / Replace Button | Action button resetting the image preview, re-enabling webcam feed or allowing a new file selection. |
| Analyze Waste Button | Primary call-to-action button; enabled once a valid image is staged; persists photo to Cloudflare R2 and navigates to the result dialog (SCR-USR-02). |

#### **2.1.2 Scan Result & Feedback Dialog (SCR-USR-02)**

![][image23]

* **Mapped Use Case:** U-01: Identify Waste via Photo (UC10), U-04: Report Incorrect AI Classification (UC13)  
  \[Content \#1: UI layout (Wireframe or Mockup for the screen)\]  
  \*\[Placeholder for UI Mockup: SCR-USR-02 — Modal/Card displaying scanned image preview, AI top prediction, confidence score badge, quick action buttons, and incorrect reporting dropdown\]\*

This screen allows the User to:

* Review the predicted waste classification, percentage confidence score, and recyclability badge.

### **5.0 Overview Table** {#5.0-overview-table}

| **JOB-02** | Reset Daily Check-in & Validate Consecutive Streak | Scheduled | Daily at 00:00 (ICT / GMT+7) | Refreshes daily check-in availability; evaluates user activity from the prior day and resets consecutive check-in streak to Day 1 if a day was missed. | **BR-GAM-09** |
| **JOB-03** | Expire Pending Handover Requests | Scheduled | Every 30 minutes | Automatically transitions pending scrap handover requests to Expired if no recycling facility accepts or rejects them within the configured SLA window. | **BR-HND-02**, **BR-NTF-02** |
| **JOB-04** | Flag Outdated Scrap Price Lists | Scheduled | Daily at 01:00 (ICT / GMT+7) | Attaches a visual "Outdated Pricing" warning badge to recycler facility profiles if their scrap buying price list has not been updated for over 30 days. | **BR-MTH-03** |
| **JOB-05** | Close Leaderboard Cycle & Reset Top Rankings | Scheduled | Periodic (Weekly / Monthly / Quarterly configured by Admin) | Archives previous leaderboard cycle rankings into historical audit logs and resets active cycle points to zero to initiate a clean competition. | **BR-GAM-07**, **BR-ADM-05** |
| **JOB-06** | Export Curated Scrap Images for AI Retraining | Scheduled | Weekly on Sunday at 02:00 (ICT) | Automatically extracts staff-verified and re-annotated misclassification images to augment the dataset pipeline for model retraining. | **BR-CLS-06**, **BR-CLS-07** |
| **JOB-07** | Purge Stale Unverified Accounts | Scheduled | Daily at 03:00 (ICT / GMT+7) | Deactivates or purges unverified draft registrations exceeding the verification timeframe to release email and phone number identities. | **BR-AUTH-01**, **BR-ADM-04** |
| **JOB-08** | Enforce Dispute Window Expiration | Scheduled | Every 60 minutes | Closes dispute submission eligibility on completed handover transactions once the statutory dispute period (over {N} days) has elapsed. | **BR-DSP-01** |
| **JOB-09** | Send Handover Appointment Reminders | Automated Event Trigger | Triggered {X} hours prior to scheduled appointment | Dispatches automated push notifications reminding both the User and the Recycler of their upcoming scrap collection handover time and location. | **BR-NTF-04**, **BR-NEG-05**, **BR-NTF-05** |
| **JOB-10** | Cancel Expired In-System VietQR Payment Orders | Scheduled | Every 5 minutes | Scans pending in-system service orders (Verified Badges, Ad-Free packages) and transitions them to Expired if uncompleted past the 15-minute countdown. | **BR-PAY-01**, **BR-PAY-02** |
| **JOB-11** | Auto-Unlock Temporarily Locked Accounts | Scheduled | Every 5 minutes | Restores normal active status for accounts temporarily locked due to consecutive failed sign-in attempts once the {M}-minute lockout cooldown elapses. | **BR-AUTH-04** |
| **JOB-12** | Expire Unused Reward Vouchers | Scheduled | Daily at 00:05 (ICT / GMT+7) | Scans redeemed merchant voucher codes and marks expired ones as Invalid to prevent fraudulent redemption at partner outlets. | **BR-GAM-05** |

### **5.1 Auto-Complete Handover Receipt (JOB-01)** {#5.1-auto-complete-handover-receipt-(job-01)}

**Trigger:** Scheduled — every 60 minutes (at the top of each hour).  
**Purpose:** Protects recycling facilities from stalled settlements by automatically closing transactions and crediting user reward points when the user takes no action within 48 hours after receipt issuance.  
**Processing steps:**

1. The system queries all handover receipts residing in Pending\_User\_Confirmation status created more than 48 hours prior to the current timestamp.  
2. For each identified receipt, the system automatically transitions the transaction status to Completed.  
3. Calculates the earned Green Seed points based on verified scrap weight and configured conversion matrices, then deposits the points into the user's reward balance (BR-GAM-01).  
4. Seals the transaction record into immutable historical transaction ledgers where further editing or deletion is strictly prohibited (BR-HND-07).  
5. Dispatches an automated push notification informing the user that their handover transaction has been auto-completed and reward points have been credited.

**Failure behavior:**

| Scenario | System behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Database unreachable | Job pauses execution, records a warning event in system operational logs, and retries on the next scheduled execution cycle. No partial data mutations occur. |
| Open dispute exists on receipt | The system skips this receipt, preserving its current state pending customer support staff adjudication; auto-completion is strictly inhibited. |

### **5.2 Reset Daily Check-in & Validate Consecutive Streak (JOB-02)** {#5.2-reset-daily-check-in-&-validate-consecutive-streak-(job-02)}

**Trigger:** Scheduled — daily at exactly 00:00 (ICT / GMT+7).  
**Purpose:** Refreshes daily check-in eligibility for the new calendar day and resets consecutive check-in streaks if a user missed checking in on the previous day.  
**Processing steps:**

1. Scans all active User and Staff accounts registered across the platform.  
2. Resets the daily check-in state flag for all accounts to Unchecked.  
3. Evaluates the most recent check-in timestamp for each user. If the user failed to perform a check-in during the preceding calendar day, the system resets their consecutive streak counter back to Day 1 pursuant to BR-GAM-09.  
4. Records the count of initialized accounts into system maintenance logs.

**Failure behavior:**

| Scenario | System behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Midnight scheduled execution outage | Upon system restoration, the job immediately verifies current calendar date checkpoints and executes compensation sweeps prior to allowing any user check-in operations. |

### **5.3 Expire Pending Handover Requests (JOB-03)** {#5.3-expire-pending-handover-requests-(job-03)}

**Trigger:** Scheduled — every 30 minutes.  
**Purpose:** Prevents scrap collection requests from remaining indefinitely unresolved when recycling facilities do not respond within configured response windows.  
**Processing steps:**

1. Scans all collection handover requests remaining in Pending status whose submission timestamp exceeds the administrative SLA timeout threshold (e.g., 24 hours).  
2. Transitions the status of qualifying requests to Expired pursuant to BR-HND-02.  
3. Dispatches informational push notifications to initiating users, advising them that their request has expired and suggesting alternative nearby recycling facilities (BR-NTF-02).

**Failure behavior:**

| Scenario | System behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Recycler accepts request during sweep | The user-driven acceptance action takes precedence; transaction transitions to Accepted, and the background job skips the record. |

### **5.4 Flag Outdated Scrap Price Lists (JOB-04)** {#5.4-flag-outdated-scrap-price-lists-(job-04)}

**Trigger:** Scheduled — daily at 01:00 AM (ICT / GMT+7).  
**Purpose:** Enforces pricing transparency by alerting users when a recycling facility has not maintained scrap purchasing rates within the past 30 days.  
**Processing steps:**

1. Evaluates all active recycling facility profile records within the platform.  
2. Compares the last updated timestamp of each facility's scrap price list against the current system date. If the delta exceeds 30 calendar days, the system attaches an Outdated Pricing Warning badge to the public facility profile (BR-MTH-03).  
3. Generates an automated portal reminder advising the facility owner to review and republish current scrap prices.

**Failure behavior:**

| Scenario | System behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Push notification service outage | Logs the error; the application of the visual warning badge on the database and public profile proceeds unaffected. |

### **5.5 Close Leaderboard Cycle & Reset Top Rankings (JOB-05)** {#5.5-close-leaderboard-cycle-&-reset-top-rankings-(job-05)}

**Trigger:** Scheduled — periodic execution at cycle conclusion configured by Administrator (Weekly, Monthly, or Quarterly).  
**Purpose:** Archives completed competition cycle rankings into permanent historical records and initializes a zero-point competition period for active participants.  
**Processing steps:**

1. Compiles and snapshots final ranking standings and cycle points into historical archive tables (BR-ADM-05).  
2. Resets cycle competition points to zero for all participants (while preserving lifetime reward wallet balances).  
3. Enforces calculation criteria: points are derived exclusively from completed, non-disputed handover transactions (BR-GAM-07).  
4. Dispatches congratulatory award notifications and honors to top leaderboard finishers.

**Failure behavior:**

| Scenario | System behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Snapshot archival fails | The job immediately aborts the point reset routine, preserves existing leaderboard standings intact, and issues a critical alert to prevent historical data loss. |

### **5.6 Export Curated Scrap Images for AI Retraining (JOB-06)** {#5.6-export-curated-scrap-images-for-ai-retraining-(job-06)}

**Trigger:** Scheduled — weekly on Sunday at 02:00 AM (ICT / GMT+7).  
**Purpose:** Extracts high-quality verified waste images re-annotated by Support Staff to feed downstream model fine-tuning workflows.  
**Processing steps:**

1. Identifies classification dispute records where Support Staff verified, resolved, and corrected item bounding boxes and category labels during the week (BR-CLS-06).  
2. Cross-references image hashes to guarantee selected samples do not exist in test benchmark splits, preventing AI data leakage (BR-CLS-07).  
3. Bundles verified image assets alongside standardized JSON annotations and synchronizes them to the training dataset storage partition.  
4. Marks processed records as exported to prevent redundant extraction in subsequent cycles.

**Failure behavior:**

| Scenario | System behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| No newly curated images available | Job completes immediately with zero operations; logs a normal informational status. |

### **5.7  Purge Stale Unverified Accounts (JOB-07)** {#5.7-purge-stale-unverified-accounts-(job-07)}

**Trigger:** Scheduled — daily at 03:00 AM (ICT / GMT+7).  
**Purpose:** Releases orphaned usernames, email addresses, and phone numbers held by abandoned registrations that failed email verification.  
**Processing steps:**

1. Scans user account entities in Unverified status whose registration creation timestamp exceeds the statutory cutoff (e.g., 7 days).  
2. Deactivates or purges draft records to liberate identity identifiers for prospective legitimate users (BR-AUTH-01).  
3. Enforces historical protection rules: accounts associated with past transactions are strictly immune from deletion (BR-ADM-04).

**Failure behavior:**

| Scenario | System behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Database write timeout | Rolls back current batch, logs warning event, and schedules retry for the subsequent night. |

### **5.8 Enforce Dispute Window Expiration (JOB-08)** {#5.8-enforce-dispute-window-expiration-(job-08)}

**Trigger:** Scheduled — every 60 minutes.  
**Purpose:** Closes dispute submission eligibility on completed handover transactions once the statutory dispute period has elapsed, preserving financial ledger stability.  
**Processing steps:**

1. Queries handover transactions in Completed status whose completion timestamp exceeds the maximum dispute eligibility window ({N} days).  
2. Transitions dispute eligibility status to Dispute\_Window\_Closed pursuant to BR-DSP-01.  
3. Deactivates the dispute initiation control within the user interfaces of both participating parties.

**Failure behavior:**

| Scenario | System behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Database connectivity interruption | Retries automatically on the subsequent execution interval with zero collateral data impact. |

### **5.9 Send Handover Appointment Reminders (JOB-09)** {#5.9-send-handover-appointment-reminders-(job-09)}

**Trigger:** Automated Event Trigger — executes {X} hours prior to scheduled appointment timestamp.  
**Purpose:** Minimizes appointment no-shows and scheduling lapses by proactively notifying both user and collector before the agreed collection slot.  
**Processing steps:**

1. Identifies collection handover agreements finalized by mutual mutual consent scheduled for fulfillment within the reminder window (BR-NEG-05).  
2. Dispatches real-time push notifications to mobile and web clients of both User and Recycler (BR-NTF-04).  
3. Formulates reminder notifications containing appointment time, address location, and waste preparation reminders, strictly omitting sensitive payment data (BR-NTF-05).

**Failure behavior:**

| Scenario | System behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| User client offline / unreachable | Push payload is retained in Firebase Cloud Messaging message queue and delivered upon client reconnect. |

### **5.10 Cancel Expired In-System VietQR Payment Orders (JOB-10)** {#5.10-cancel-expired-in-system-vietqr-payment-orders-(job-10)}

**Trigger:** Scheduled — every 5 minutes.  
**Purpose:** Automatically cancels dynamic VietQR payment orders that exceed the 15-minute countdown window without payment confirmation, ensuring inventory and order integrity.  
**Processing steps:**

1. Scans pending in-system service orders (e.g., Verified Green Badges, Ad-Free subscriptions) remaining in Pending\_Payment status older than 15 minutes.  
2. Transitions order status to Expired and deactivates the associated dynamic VietQR code pursuant to BR-PAY-01.  
3. Records session termination in the payment ledger to prevent accidental post-expiry service provisioning (BR-PAY-02).

**Failure behavior:**

| Scenario | System behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Bank webhook arrives during cancellation | System verifies bank transfer timestamp: if payment was confirmed before the 15-minute threshold, payment takes precedence and service is activated. |

### **5.11  Auto-Unlock Temporarily Locked Accounts (JOB-11)** {#5.11-auto-unlock-temporarily-locked-accounts-(job-11)}

**Trigger:** Scheduled — every 5 minutes.  
**Purpose:** Restores sign-in access automatically for accounts temporarily locked due to consecutive invalid credentials once the lockout period has expired.  
**Processing steps:**

1. Queries all account records residing in Temporarily\_Locked status resulting from exceeding failed password attempt thresholds.  
2. Evaluates the lockout timestamp against current system time; if the elapsed duration meets or exceeds {M} minutes (pursuant to BR-AUTH-04), resets failed attempt count to zero.  
3. Restores account status to Active, enabling the user to resume normal authentication attempts.

**Failure behavior:**

| Scenario | System behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| No locked accounts identified | Job finishes cleanly with zero database modifications. |

### **5.12 Expire Unused Reward Vouchers (JOB-12)** {#5.12-expire-unused-reward-vouchers-(job-12)}

**Trigger:** Scheduled — daily at 00:05 AM (ICT / GMT+7).  
**Purpose:** Invalidates redeemed merchant vouchers that have passed their designated expiration date, preventing invalid redemption disputes with partner vendors.  
**Processing steps:**

1. Evaluates all redeemed voucher records held in user reward wallets that remain in Unredeemed status.  
2. Compares voucher expiration validity dates against the current date; transitions expired codes to Invalid\_Expired pursuant to BR-GAM-05.  
3. Updates the user wallet view, displaying expired vouchers with a muted visual state and an "Expired" indicator.

**Failure behavior:**

| Scenario | System behavior |
| :---- | :---- |
| Network timeout during status batch update | Job captures warning log and schedules a catch-up execution batch. |

# **IV. Non-Functional Requirements** {#iv.-non-functional-requirements}

## **1\. External Interfaces** {#1.-external-interfaces}

The EcoLink system communicates properly with end users, client devices, internal services, and designated external third-party service providers through the following standardized interfaces:

| ID | Interface | Description | Protocol / Format |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| EI-01 | User Interface (Web) | Responsive React web application serving Guest, User, Recycler, Staff, and Administrator actors. Access to client hardware features (device camera for AI waste capture and Geolocation API for GPS recycler discovery) requires explicit runtime user consent. | HTTPS, HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript |
| EI-02 | AI Classification Service | Internal inference microservice hosting the self-trained computer vision waste classification model. The backend transmits image payloads over a secure private network and receives top-N predicted categories, material groups, and confidence scores. | REST / JSON (Internal Virtual Network) |
| EI-03 | Map & Geolocation Service | Integrates with map service provider (OpenStreetMap / Google Maps) and PostGIS database extension for address geocoding, interactive map rendering, distance computation, and spatial radius query execution. | REST (Map Provider), SQL (PostGIS) |
| EI-04 | Object Storage (Cloudflare R2) | Cloud object storage storing waste photos, handover receipt evidence, dispute proof photos, facility business licenses, user avatars, and blog media. Relational database stores unique object keys only. | S3-Compatible API (Private Bucket) |
| EI-05 | Google OAuth 2.0 | External authentication provider for Single Sign-On (SSO) and quick account registration. The system verifies identity tokens directly with Google and validates the email\_verified claim on every login (BR-AUTH-02, BR-AUTH-07). | OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect (HTTPS) |
| EI-06 | Gmail / SMTP Mail Service | Automated email delivery service used to dispatch account verification links, password reset links/OTPs, handover status alerts, dispute resolution conclusions, and periodic survey invitations. | SMTP over TLS (Port 587\) |
| EI-07 | Real-time Messaging Channel | Full-duplex real-time communication channel powering negotiation chat (NEG) between User and Recycler and delivering instantaneous in-app system notifications (NTF). | WebSocket (WSS) with polling fallback |
| EI-08 | Database Interface | High-performance relational database storage with PostGIS extension for structured business entities, relational constraints, transaction records, and spatial queries. | TCP / TLS (Private Virtual Network) |
| EI-09 | Data Export Interface | Generates downloadable business analytics, transaction ledgers, and environmental statistics reports for administrative audit and external reporting. | .xlsx / .csv (UTF-8 Encoded) |

## **2\. Quality Attributes** {#2.-quality-attributes}

The required software quality attributes and behavioral characteristics of the EcoLink platform are specified below across distinct quality dimensions:

### **2.1 Usability** {#2.1-usability}

| ID | Requirement | Measure |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| NFR-USA-01 | A first-time User must be able to complete the core flow ('scan waste \-\> view sorting guidance') without formal training. | \<= 3 operational steps; \>= 90% of test users complete unaided on first attempt |
| NFR-USA-02 | All primary actions (AI scan, upload photo, view sorting guide, find nearby recycler, create handover request, daily check-in) must be directly accessible from the main dashboard. | \<= 2 clicks or taps from the home landing view |
| NFR-USA-03 | System error, confirmation, and validation messages must be presented in clear, non-technical language and conform strictly to the System Messages catalog (MSG-\*). | 100% of user-facing dialogs; system stack traces and database errors are strictly suppressed |
| NFR-USA-04 | The user interface must provide comprehensive bilingual language support for Vietnamese (default) and English. | Instantaneous toggle across all screens without loss of entered form data or page reload |
| NFR-USA-05 | The web application interface must provide a consistent, responsive layout supporting desktop, tablet, and mobile browsers. | Seamless viewport scaling across widths ranging from 360 px to 1920 px |
| NFR-USA-06 | The application interface must adhere to international accessibility and readability guidelines. | Conforms to WCAG 2.1 AA standards; all interactive touch targets are at least 44x44 px |
| NFR-USA-07 | Long-running asynchronous operations (AI image classification, media upload, report generation) must display active visual progress indicators. | Visual progress state displayed within \<= 200 ms of user trigger; includes cancel/retry options |
| NFR-USA-08 | A Recycler must be able to review incoming handover requests, negotiate terms, create digital receipts, and confirm completion in a concise flow. | \<= 5 steps; \<= 2 minutes total operational time for a trained Recycler |
| NFR-USA-09 | Operations Staff must be able to compose rich-text educational blog articles and submit them for administrative review without technical formatting knowledge. | \<= 5 steps from clicking 'New Post' to final submission for Admin review |

### **2.2 Performance** {#2.2-performance}

| ID | Requirement | Target | Condition |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| NFR-PER-01 | AI classification response latency | Result returned within \<= 5 seconds (95th percentile); hard timeout at 15 seconds | Image size \<= 10 MB, up to 100 concurrent classification requests |
| NFR-PER-02 | Web page initial load time | All non-media web views render fully within \<= 3 seconds (95th percentile) | Up to 100 concurrent active users on standard 4G mobile connection |
| NFR-PER-03 | Nearby-recycler spatial search latency | Spatial search results and map marker coordinates returned within \<= 2 seconds | Search radius up to 20 km, up to 100 concurrent spatial search queries |
| NFR-PER-04 | Standard transactional API response latency | System acknowledges submission (login, create request, confirm receipt, check-in, redeem) within \<= 2 seconds (P95) | Up to 100 concurrent users active simultaneously |
| NFR-PER-05 | Real-time negotiation chat message delivery | End-to-end message transmission latency \<= 2 seconds | Standard network connectivity between User and Recycler |
| NFR-PER-06 | Dashboard analytics rendering & report export | Dashboard metrics render within \<= 5 seconds; report generation completes within \<= 30 seconds | Aggregated datasets containing up to 100,000 transaction records |
| NFR-PER-07 | Concurrent active user capacity | System remains fully operational with zero request loss or stability degradation | 100 concurrent active users on single-server deployment baseline |
| NFR-PER-08 | Sorting catalog & leaderboard lookup | Active sorting policies and leaderboard rankings retrieved within \<= 2 seconds | High-concurrency cached read paths under normal system load |

### **2.3 Security** {#2.3-security}

| ID | Requirement | Description | Related Rules |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| NFR-SEC-01 | Mandatory authentication gate | All application screens and API endpoints require authenticated sessions, excluding public landing pages, waste catalog search, approved blog posts, login, registration, and password recovery. | BR-AUTH-08 |
| NFR-SEC-02 | Cryptographic password protection | Passwords must never be stored in plaintext or reversible encryption; stored using salted adaptive cryptographic hashing (bcrypt or Argon2). Minimum length 8 characters including uppercase letters and digits. | BR-AUTH-04 |
| NFR-SEC-03 | Account lockout protection | Accounts are temporarily locked for 15 minutes after 5 consecutive failed sign-in attempts to prevent brute-force credential stuffing; automatically unlocked by background job JOB-01. | BR-AUTH-04, JOB-01 |
| NFR-SEC-04 | Role-based access control (RBAC) | Enforces strict server-side authorization and separation of duties across Guest, User, Recycler, Staff, and Administrator roles in accordance with the Permission Matrix. | BR-AUTH-08, BR-ADM-02 |
| NFR-SEC-05 | Transport layer encryption | All client-to-server and inter-service communications must be encrypted in transit using HTTPS/TLS 1.2+ with HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) headers enforced. | Industry Standard |
| NFR-SEC-06 | Secure session lifecycle | JWT access token lifetime is limited to \<= 60 minutes \[TBD\]; all active user sessions are invalidated immediately upon password change, account suspension, or deactivation. | BR-AUTH-05, BR-AUTH-06 |
| NFR-SEC-07 | Anti-enumeration defenses | Authentication failure and password recovery responses provide identical generic messages regardless of whether the target username or email exists in the database. | BR-AUTH-03, BR-AUTH-06 |
| NFR-SEC-08 | API rate limiting & abuse mitigation | Sensitive public endpoints enforce strict rate limiting: AI scan and recycler search \<= 30 req/min/user; password reset restricted per email/IP; login restricted per IP. | BR-AUTH-09 |
| NFR-SEC-09 | File upload sanitization & inspection | All uploaded media files are inspected for valid magic numbers, restricted to JPG/PNG, capped at \<= 10 MB, and stripped of sensitive EXIF geolocation metadata upon ingestion. | BR-CLS-01 |
| NFR-SEC-10 | Private object storage authorization | Stored media files (waste photos, receipts, dispute proof) remain in private buckets, served strictly via short-lived signed URLs generated after server-side access verification. | BR-CLS-08, BR-DSP-06 |
| NFR-SEC-11 | Location data privacy protection | Precise user GPS coordinates are utilized solely on the server side to compute distances and are never exposed to Recyclers. Exact pickup address is shared only after request acceptance. | BR-MTH-05, BR-HND-08 |
| NFR-SEC-12 | Application vulnerability defenses | Application is hardened against OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities: parameterized queries prevent SQL injection, strict output encoding prevents XSS, and anti-forgery tokens prevent CSRF attacks. | OWASP Top 10 |
| NFR-SEC-13 | Secrets & credentials management | Database credentials, cloud storage keys, and OAuth client secrets must reside in isolated environment variables or secret vaults; hardcoding in source code is strictly prohibited. | Industry Standard |
| NFR-SEC-14 | Immutable audit logging | All administrative operations, role modifications, recycler approvals/rejections, dispute decisions, blog approvals, and data exports are logged to an append-only audit trail; retained for 90 days. | BR-ADM-05, JOB-02 |
| NFR-SEC-15 | Transaction record immutability | Negotiation chat transcripts, accepted offer snapshots, confirmed receipts, and dispute arbitration evidence cannot be edited or deleted by any user or administrator. | BR-NEG-01, BR-HND-07 |
| NFR-SEC-16 | OAuth token server-side verification | Google OAuth ID tokens must be cryptographically validated with Google public keys on every login; accounts registered via Google default strictly to the User role. | BR-AUTH-07 |
| NFR-SEC-17 | QR code redirect safety | Scanned QR codes must validate against internal system-issued identifiers; external URL redirections are strictly blocked to prevent open redirect vulnerabilities. | BR-SRT-05 |
| NFR-SEC-18 | Notification data protection | Automated email and push notifications must never contain sensitive authorization tokens or full contact details, except one-time account verification or password reset links. | BR-NTF-05 |
| NFR-SEC-19 | Personal data regulatory compliance | Data collection complies with Vietnam Personal Data Protection Decree (Decree 13/2023/ND-CP); user accounts with historical transactions are deactivated rather than hard-deleted. | BR-ADM-04, BR-ADM-06 |
| NFR-SEC-20 | Content moderation integrity gate | Blog articles drafted by Staff remain completely inaccessible to public users until an Administrator formally reviews and approves the submission. | BR-ADM-08 |

###  **2.4 Reliability & Availability** {#2.4-reliability-&-availability}

| ID | Requirement | Target | Condition |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| NFR-REL-01 | Overall system availability | \>= 99.0% service uptime measured monthly | Excludes announced scheduled maintenance windows (\<= 4 hours/month) |
| NFR-REL-02 | AI classification fault tolerance | Displays user-friendly notification (MSG-CLS-05); auto-retries once; prompts user to retry or browse waste catalog manually | AI inference microservice temporarily unreachable or times out (\> 15 s) |
| NFR-REL-03 | Handover state transition integrity | Strict one-way lifecycle progression (Pending \-\> Accepted \-\> Scheduled \-\> Completed); states are never lost, skipped, or duplicated | Concurrent User and Recycler updates handled via database transactions and optimistic locking |
| NFR-REL-04 | Atomic points & reward transactions | Deducting Eco-points, updating voucher inventory stock, and issuing unique voucher codes execute as a single atomic transaction; point balance cannot be negative | High-concurrency voucher redemptions and daily check-in events |
| NFR-REL-05 | Graceful third-party degradation | Transient failures of external services (Google Maps, Gmail SMTP, WebSockets) must not crash core web applications or block scan/handover flows | External third-party API outage or network disruption |
| NFR-REL-06 | Reliable email notification delivery | Failed email transmissions are logged and retried automatically up to {N}=3 times; delivery failures never roll back core business transactions | Temporary SMTP gateway disruption or mail server timeout (BR-NTF-06) |
| NFR-REL-07 | Background worker resilience | Scheduled background workers (account unlock JOB-01, log cleanup JOB-02, reminder dispatch, request expiry) are idempotent with automatic retry and error alerts | Worker execution failures or temporary database timeouts |

###  **2.5 Scalability** {#2.5-scalability}

* NFR-SCA-01: Microservice AI Architecture The AI Classification Service is deployed and scaled independently in an isolated container/microservice, ensuring heavy computer-vision inference loads do not degrade web and transaction responsiveness.  
* NFR-SCA-02: Spatial Index Optimization PostGIS GiST spatial indexing on facility coordinates ensures nearest-neighbor and radius queries execute within \<= 2 seconds even as the directory scales to over 10,000 recycling partners.  
* NFR-SCA-03: Stateless Backend Services The .NET API backend is designed to be fully stateless, enabling seamless horizontal scale-out across multiple container instances behind a reverse proxy/load balancer.  
* NFR-SCA-04: Database Capacity Sizing The PostgreSQL database schema and indexing strategy are optimized to handle up to 100,000 registered users and 1,000,000 waste scan records without structural redesign.  
* NFR-SCA-05: Server-Side Pagination All high-volume data listings (scan history, accounts, transaction logs, reviews, audit logs) enforce server-side pagination with a default page size of 20 items.

### **2.6 Maintainability** {#2.6-maintainability}

* NFR-MNT-01: Layered Architectural Pattern Backend application is structured following clean layered architecture (Controller â€  
* NFR-MNT-02: Automated Test Coverage Core business rules (waste classification mapping, spatial filtering, handover status machine, gamification point calculation) maintain automated unit test coverage of at least 70%.  
* NFR-MNT-03: Centralized Dynamic Configuration Waste categories, sorting policies, gamification parameters (daily point cap, streak bonuses, tree upgrade thresholds), AI confidence threshold, lockout rules, and deviation limits are configurable via Admin UI without code redeployment.  
* NFR-MNT-04: Parameterization Governance All configurable threshold placeholders {N}, {M}, {X} defined across business rules are maintained in a centralized configuration store.  
* NFR-MNT-05: Structured Diagnostic Logging Implements structured JSON logging with unique correlation IDs across all requests, background jobs, and error events to accelerate troubleshooting.  
* NFR-MNT-06: Continuous Integration & Version Control Codebase is maintained in Git repositories with mandatory peer code reviews and an automated CI pipeline executing build verification and unit test suites.  
* NFR-MNT-07: API Documentation & Versioning All REST APIs are documented according to OpenAPI/Swagger standards and versioned explicitly (e.g., /api/v1) to ensure backward compatibility; database schema changes are managed via versioned migration scripts.

### **2.7 Compatibility & Portability** {#2.7-compatibility-&-portability}

* NFR-CMP-01: Cross-Browser Compatibility Web application renders consistently and functions fully on the latest two major releases of Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Microsoft Edge, and Apple Safari.  
* NFR-CMP-02: Mobile Browser & Device Capabilities Device camera and GPS features operate reliably on iOS Safari and Android Chrome; manual photo selection and manual address input provided as seamless fallbacks.  
* NFR-CMP-03: Infrastructure Agnostic Portability Application backend is packaged as Docker containers, allowing deployment to any standard Linux cloud environment supporting .NET and PostgreSQL without vendor lock-in.  
* NFR-CMP-04: Object Storage Interoperability Cloud storage interactions utilize standard S3-compatible APIs, allowing cloud object storage providers to be switched without application code modifications.  
* NFR-CMP-05: Localization & International Standards System enforces UTF-8 character encoding supporting full Vietnamese diacritics. Timestamps are stored in UTC and presented in UTC+7 (Indochina Time). Currency values are displayed in VND for reference only.

### **2.8 Data Backup & Recovery** {#2.8-data-backup-&-recovery}

| ID | Requirement | Target |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| NFR-BCK-01 | Automated database backup | Full automated database backup executed every 24 hours; backup snapshots retained for \>= 7 days in secure isolated storage. |
| NFR-BCK-02 | Object storage redundancy | Cross-region replication or object versioning enabled on Cloudflare R2 for waste photos, receipts, licenses, and blog media. |
| NFR-BCK-03 | Recovery Point Objective (RPO) | RPO \<= 24 hours of operational transactional data loss in the event of catastrophic primary datacenter failure. |
| NFR-BCK-04 | Recovery Time Objective (RTO) | Core platform restorable and fully operational within RTO \<= 4 hours following critical hardware or cloud disruption. |
| NFR-BCK-05 | Disaster recovery drill validation | Automated database backup restoration test executed at least once per release cycle to verify snapshot viability. |
| NFR-BCK-06 | Permanent business record retention | User accounts, completed handover transactions, receipts, negotiation chats, and disputes are retained permanently; audit logs retained for 90 days. |

###  **2.9 AI Model Quality** {#2.9-ai-model-quality}

| ID | Requirement | Target | Condition |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| NFR-AI-01 | Classification accuracy benchmark | Top-1 accuracy \>= 85%; Top-3 accuracy \>= 95% | Evaluated on held-out test dataset covering all supported recyclable waste classes |
| NFR-AI-02 | Low-confidence uncertainty handling | Predictions with confidence below Admin-configured threshold (default 60%) flagged as 'uncertain' (MSG-CLS-04); user must confirm or select manually | Enforced on every AI scan request (BR-CLS-03) |
| NFR-AI-03 | Zero-downtime model update cycle | Model retraining and container redeployment execute without downtime to main web application; instant rollback to previous version supported | Retrained using Staff-verified feedback data queue |
| NFR-AI-04 | Inference traceability & versioning | Each classification record persists model version and confidence score for auditing and longitudinal performance tracking | Stored permanently with user scan history |
| NFR-AI-05 | Dataset partition integrity | Only Staff-reviewed and labeled images enter datasets; strict automated check ensures zero sample overlap between training and validation sets | Enforced by system on dataset update (BR-CLS-06, BR-CLS-07) |
| NFR-AI-06 | Out-of-Distribution (OOD) rejection | Non-waste or unidentifiable items return informative failure (MSG-CLS-05) instead of false confident prediction; unmapped predictions are suppressed | OOD, blurry, or non-waste image inputs (BR-CLS-02) |
| NFR-AI-07 | Operational accuracy monitoring | Real-time classification accuracy, misclassification report rate, and category distribution displayed on Admin dashboard (A-01) | Continuous production monitoring reviewed monthly |
| NFR-AI-08 | Feedback traceability loop | Every misclassification report links source image, AI-predicted label, and user-suggested label into the Staff labeling queue | Enforced on every report submission (BR-CLS-05) |

###  **2.10 Auditability & Data Integrity** {#2.10-auditability-&-data-integrity}

* NFR-AUD-01: End-to-End Handover Traceability Every recycling trade is auditable from initial request creation, counter-offers, confirmed appointment time, on-site weighing photos, to final receipt confirmation.  
* NFR-AUD-02: Non-Custodial Financial Clarification EcoLink strictly records transaction quantities and reference values; the system does not handle, transfer, or escrow funds. Actual settlements occur directly between User and Recycler.  
* NFR-AUD-03: Referential Data Protection Categories, accounts, and historical records with transaction ties cannot be deleted from the database; only deactivation is permitted (BR-SRT-04, BR-ADM-04).  
* NFR-AUD-04: Dispute Accountability Every dispute outcome issued by Operations Staff must record a formal ruling recommendation and rationale, ensuring explainable moderation (BR-DSP-04).  
* NFR-AUD-05: Read-Only Dashboard Metrics High-level analytics cards and environmental tonnage summaries are computed strictly from completed and verified transactions (BR-ADM-07).

### **2.11 Legal & Compliance** {#2.11-legal-&-compliance}

* NFR-LEG-01: Terms of Service & Privacy Policy Users and Recyclers must explicitly review and accept terms of service during registration; explicit runtime consent is requested for camera and GPS access.  
* NFR-LEG-02: Personal Data Protection Compliance Adheres to Vietnam Decree 13/2023/ND-CP on Personal Data Protection and the Law on Cybersecurity; all exported data files anonymize personally identifiable information.  
* NFR-LEG-03: Community Standards & Content Moderation Public blog posts and community reviews are subject to platform moderation; Staff and Admin possess authorities to remove abusive or fraudulent entries (BR-RVW-03, BR-ADM-08).
